[chat-core] Switch JmapUri object references from jmap: to urn:jmap:
Spec (80ae683, 57243ea): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md L1845-1866: "jmap-urn = \"urn:jmap:\" segment *( \":\" segment ) / segment = 1*( ALPHA / DIGIT / \"-\" / \"_\" )" ... "2. An object URN type: a type name registered in the \"JMAP Object URN Types\" registry ({{JMAP-CHAT-CALENDARS}}). The rest of the name is `<accountId>:<objectId>`" ... "the NSS is compared case-sensitively". Commit 80ae683: "jmap: links replaced by ... object URNs with a new IANA registry"; spec HEAD example `urn:jmap:calendarevent:A13824:E6B2`.
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:1-19 (module doc: private-use `jmap:` scheme); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:155-160 FromStr (requires first segment "jmap"); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:176 Display (writes "jmap:{type}:{acct}"); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:29,33,63-67 (doc example and error strings); crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/jmap_uri.rs, tests/chat_calendars.rs, tests/chat_tasks.rs ("jmap:" fixtures)
Now: JmapUri parses and emits `jmap:<type>:<acct>:<obj>`, so a spec URN `urn:jmap:calendarevent:A:E` fails with NotJmapScheme, and our emitted references are not URNs.
Change: Parse a `urn:jmap:` prefix (NID compare case-insensitive per RFC 8141; NSS case-sensitive) and emit `urn:jmap:<type>:...`. Update the docs and the error strings. The chat-calendars and chat-tasks drafts are the primary source; chat-00 defines the namespace.

[chat-ext] Replace jmap: URI with urn:jmap: object URN in JmapUri
Spec (80ae683, 57243ea): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-calendars-00.md:96-104 "jmap-object-urn = \"urn:jmap:\" type-name \":\" account-id \":\" object-id; type-name = 1*( %x61-7A / DIGIT ) ; registered in \"JMAP Object URN Types\"; account-id = 1*255id-char; object-id = 1*255id-char"; :108 "A type name never equals the first segment after `urn:jmap:` of any other URN assigned under `urn:jmap:`: the capability URNs (such as `chat` ...) and the `urn:jmap:chat:cap:*` MessageAction and Endpoint types"; :181 "`urn:jmap:calendarevent:<accountId>:<eventId>`"; :271 "`urn:jmap:principal:<accountId>:<principalId>`"; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00.md:191 "A JMAP object URN ... of type `task`, in the form `urn:jmap:task:<accountId>:<taskId>`"
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:1-13 (module docs: private-use jmap: scheme, tasks extra segment); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:36-40 (object_ids: Vec<Id>); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:93-113 (new accepts 1..n object ids); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:155-171 (FromStr requires scheme "jmap", accepts trailing segments); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:174-178 (Display writes "jmap:..."); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:46-47,61-67 (NotJmapScheme / error text); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/tasks.rs:16-17,34-36,74-89 (JmapUri::task_ids returns (taskListId, taskId) from 2-segment form); crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/jmap_uri.rs:12-98; crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/chat_tasks.rs:228-250; crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/chat_calendars.rs:139,197,202
Now: Parses and renders "jmap:<type>:<acct>:<id>[:<id>...]"; a spec-conformant "urn:jmap:calendarevent:A1:E1" fails with NotJmapScheme, and the code emits "jmap:..." strings peers no longer recognise. The task form is jmap:task:<acct>:<taskListId>:<taskId>, but the new form has no taskListId. Because the type is only checked as lowercase alnum, "urn:jmap:chat:cap:task" would parse once the prefix is changed (type "chat"), which the collision rule is meant to rule out.
Change: Parse and render "urn:jmap:<type>:<accountId>:<objectId>" with exactly one object-id ("urn" and NID "jmap" matched case-insensitively per RFC 8141). Reject a type that collides with assigned urn:jmap: first segments (at least "chat", "did", "cid", "vtc", "scene"), or accept only registered types (calendarevent, principal, task). Collapse object_ids to a single object_id. Replace task_ids() with a single-id accessor (or drop it in favour of data_type() == "task" plus object_id()), and update JMAP_URI_TASK_TYPE docs. Update the three test files to the new draft text as oracle.
Verifier correction: As proposed: parse and render urn:jmap:<type>:<accountId>:<objectId> with exactly one object-id, and drop the task taskListId segment and task_ids(). Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[chat-core] JmapUri: accept exactly one object-id (drop tasks multi-segment form)
Spec (42c244b): draft-atwood-jmap-object-uri-00.md L71-77: "jmap-object-uri = \"jmap:\" type-name \":\" account-id \":\" object-id / type-name = 1*( %x61-7A / DIGIT ) / account-id = 1*255id-char / object-id = 1*255id-char"; L96: "A receiver treats a `jmap` URI that matches no form it implements as unresolvable."; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00.md L191: "in the form `jmap:task:<accountId>:<taskId>`"
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:36-40 (object_ids: Vec<Id>); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:81-113 (new() takes Vec, accepts 1..n ids); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:125-136 (object_id() = last; object_ids()); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:166-170 (FromStr collects all trailing segments); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:174-178 (Display writes every segment); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/tasks.rs:16-17,34-36,74-89 (JmapUri::task_ids returns (taskListId, taskId) from 5-segment form); crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/jmap_uri.rs:36-45,52,110 (task multi-segment fixtures); crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/chat_tasks.rs:228-250; crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/tests/outbound.rs:263 (uri "urn:jmap:task:A1:T1", old URN form); CHANGELOG.md:685
Now: Parses and renders jmap:<type>:<acct>:<id>[:<id>...]; "jmap:task:A1:TL1:T9" parses successfully and task_ids() yields a taskListId, a form that matches no jmap-object-uri production. Scheme, type grammar, Id charset/length (crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:191-211) and case-insensitive scheme (jmap_uri.rs:158) already conform.
Change: Make object_id a single Id: new(data_type, account_id, object_id); FromStr rejects any segment after the object-id (new error variant or reuse InvalidObjectId); remove object_ids() and task_ids() (callers use data_type()==JMAP_URI_TASK_TYPE + object_id()). Re-cite module/type docs to draft-atwood-jmap-object-uri-00 §JMAP Object URIs instead of the "private-use" calendars-draft scheme (jmap_uri.rs:1-13,19). Update the test fixtures to the new drafts as oracle; change outbound.rs:263 fixture to jmap:task:A1:T1 or an https URI. Public API break; CHANGELOG.

[chat-ext] JmapUri must use one object id; drop the 5-segment task form
Spec (42c244b): draft-atwood-jmap-object-uri-00.md L71-77: "jmap-object-uri = \"jmap:\" type-name \":\" account-id \":\" object-id" ... "object-id = 1*255id-char"; draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00.md L191: "A JMAP object URI ({{JMAP-OBJECT-URI}}) of type `task`, in the form `jmap:task:<accountId>:<taskId>`, referencing a Task on the named account."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:1-13 (module doc: private-use scheme, tasks extra segment); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:36-40 object_ids: Vec<Id>; crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:84-113 new(.., Vec<Id>); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:132-136 object_ids(); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/jmap_uri.rs:166-170 FromStr accepts any number of trailing segments; crate-jmap-chat-types/src/tasks.rs:16-17,74-89 JmapUri::task_ids; crate-jmap-chat-types/tests/jmap_uri.rs:36-52,106-115; tests/chat_tasks.rs:228-250
Now: The parser accepts jmap:<type>:<acct>:<id>[:<id>...] and renders the multi-segment form; task_ids() reads (taskListId, taskId) from jmap:task:A:TL:T. That form is not a valid jmap-object-uri, and a spec-form jmap:task:A:T yields task_ids() == None. The `jmap` scheme itself is correct (42c244b reverted the urn:jmap: move).
Change: Keep the scheme `jmap` (case-insensitive). Require exactly one object-id (reject extra segments), collapse object_ids to object_id, and change new() to take a single Id. Remove task_ids() and the extra-segment docs; consumers use data_type()=="task" plus object_id(). Update the module doc to cite draft-atwood-jmap-object-uri-00. Update the tests to the new draft text. Restricting to registered types (calendar, calendarevent, principal, task, tasklist, filenode) is optional hardening, because the spec says an unknown form is just unresolvable.","title":"JmapUri: exactly one object-id per object-uri-00"}
